text:
Marathon Petroleum edged up 0.89% today, continuing a strong two-week run of nearly 9%. The stock's gains reflect a volatile geopolitical environment around oil markets: crude prices have climbed sharply (US oil at $97.26/barrel, up significantly from recent lows), and refineries are running at 97.8% capacity, suggesting tight supply and strong margins for oil processors like Marathon. Recent headlines about strikes in the Strait of Hormuz, ongoing Iran-U.S. tensions, and competing diplomatic efforts are keeping oil prices elevated and uncertain.

The broader pattern here is that refiner stocks tend to benefit when crude prices rise but product demand remains steady—and with gasoline and diesel storage levels in normal ranges, refiners can move their output. However, this rally also hinges on geopolitical risk remaining elevated; if diplomacy succeeds and oil prices fall sharply (as Trump suggested they might after midterm elections), refiner margins could compress quickly, which explains why Marathon has seesawed between $387 and $399 over the last two weeks.
